decisive_items: multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular and periaqueductal regions, dorsomedial thalami, medial temporal lobes, caudate nuclei, and brainstem, with diffusion restriction and low ADC values
diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar cord
febrile, and his condition deteriorated into respiratory distress requiring intubation
response.rationale: Acute febrile encephalomyelitis with symmetric deep gray/white matter lesions, spinal cord involvement, and rapid progression best fits ADEM. R7 captures the full imaging and clinical picture; R4 is a duplicate label with less complete support.

rejected.why: Substance use history is nonspecific; no toxic exposure or characteristic imaging pattern for toxic encephalopathy.
NMOSD typically shows optic neuritis or longitudinally extensive myelitis with distinct brain lesions; symmetric periventricular/thalamic involvement and diffusion restriction are atypical.
Same as R2; lacks optic nerve involvement and has atypical brain MRI pattern for NMOSD.
MS is typically relapsing-remitting with periventricular ovoid lesions; symmetric deep gray matter and diffuse cord involvement with fever are more consistent with ADEM.
Transverse myelitis alone cannot explain the extensive bilateral brain lesions and encephalopathy.
